referents.why: The third masculine singular suffix on steadfast love (his loving devotion) can only be the LORD, the one masculine singular referent in the verse; the parallel clause makes the loyalty God's.
referents.category: possessive suffix to the divine name

referents.why: Second person plural imperative (give thanks): the 'you' is the audience the call is addressed to. No candidate in the verse is second person plural; the psalmist is the speaker, not the addressee.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to an unnamed audience

links.why: Give thanks, for (ki) he is good: the ki after the command gives its ground. A plain 'and' would not do this; the reason is stated.

The second ki opens a parallel line that restates the praise in other words (good; loyalty endures forever), joined by a semicolon in the translation. It is not a reason for the goodness, so the pair is recorded as a parallel group instead.
links.category: second ki line read as parallel, not cause

groups.why: The builder put cl1 under role part, which the imperative kind does not have. The clauses giving the ground of the command are the couplet, so the basis is the new parallel group.
groups.category: invalid member role on imperative group

groups.why: The sender of the psalm's words is its voice (the psalmist), not the LORD who is spoken of; the LORD is the topic. Psalm 107 has no superscription, so cl0 is not a heading and does not fill the frame role; the command is part of what the psalm says.
groups.category: writer is the psalm's voice, not its subject

groups.why: Two lines answering each other in the same form, both opening with ki, the second restating the first in other words. Their subjects differ (the LORD; his steadfast love), so there is no group_subject.

cant_tell.what: Who the plural 'you' of the call to thank is
cant_tell.why: The verse names no audience; the hearers of the psalm are not identified inside the verse.
